title: Reimagine density-aware column handoff and microinteractions for virtualized tables
creator: Sofia Reyes
description:
Objective: Create a cohesive interaction model and visual token mappings for virtualized tables that make column resizing, drag handoff, sorting and filtering discoverable and reliable across compact, default, and spacious density modes.

Background: Our existing table work has focused on column affordances and density presets, but feedback from PM and engineering shows friction when users resize or move columns under heavy virtualization (rows loading/unloading) and when density switches mid-session. Edge cases produce janky pointer handoffs, lost focus, and confusion about sort/filter state.

Problem statement: Users need a clear, low-latency interaction model for column adjustments and sorting/filtering that: 1) survives virtualization boundaries (no lost gestures when rows remount), 2) adapts visually and spatially across density modes, and 3) exposes sorting/filtering feedback without overwhelming compact mode.

Proposal summary: Design a "handoff rail" and density-aware microinteraction system:
- Introduce a lightweight interaction rail that appears on hover/focus and extends the resize/drag target area during active gestures.
- Implement a small, persistent sort/filter chip in column headers that collapses progressively with density (icon-only in compact, icon+label in default, full label+hint in spacious).
- Define token sets for spacing, hit targets, and animation durations per density mode to keep motion consistent when virtualization triggers row reflows.
- Prefetch and hold header mounts during active drags to avoid unmount remount flicker (coord with engineering runtime team).

Deliverables:
- Finalized header interaction spec with annotated diagrams
- Token table mapping spacing, pointer-target sizes, and micro-animation timing for compact/default/spacious modes
- Figma prototype demonstrating drag-resize handoff across density switch and live sorting chips
- Accessibility guidance and keyboard/focus flows for column resize and sort operations
- Implementation notes for runtime (KV cache interaction and header mount hold)

Audience: Design system team, frontend engineering (table runtime), product managers for Console and Redwood Console consumers, accessibility reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: Header rail appears on hover or keyboard focus and increases effective pointer target by at least 24px without breaking layout
Sort/filter chip adapts across density modes: compact (icon), default (icon + short label), spacious (icon + label + hint)
During an active drag/resize the header element remains mounted for the duration of the gesture (engineering validated by integration test)
Prototype demonstrates no visible jank when toggling density mid-gesture in at least two browsers (Chrome, Safari)
Accessibility: keyboard-only users can resize columns with modifier keys and receive clear ARIA announcements for sort/filter state changes
decisions: Use a non-invasive hover rail (semi-transparent) rather than enlarging the entire header to minimize layout shift
Collapse sort/filter affordance progressively instead of hiding completely to preserve discoverability in compact mode
Animation durations will be density-proportional: compact: 100ms, default: 140ms, spacious: 180ms to match perceived speed
Coordinate mount-hold behavior with runtime team instead of trying a purely CSS fallback due to virtualization lifecycle complexity
tradeoffs: Mount-hold increases memory surface on long-running gestures but prevents jank; engineering will monitor memory/GC metrics
Rail visibility on hover adds a visual element that could be noisy; mitigated by low-opacity and motion reduction setting
Progressive collapse of the chip risks icon ambiguity in rare locales; accepted in favor of consistent compact density footprint
